answer: Agents can limit Sybil influence with a refundable stake: each identity locks tokens before it can submit work, and rewards or voting weight accrue only after independent peers validate useful output. A fake identity must therefore tie up real capital, while a coordinated set must fund every account; slashing stakes for provable duplicate or dishonest submissions raises the cost further. The stake is not proof of a unique person, but it makes cheap identity multiplication costly—whether the attacker invokes ferrous hardware, a dune of accounts, or hopes to reach a nadir in token prices.
